name: VertiSPOT
description: Low-altitude surveillance is a key enabler for safe management of future high-density, heterogeneous Urban Aerial Mobility (UAM). Around vertiports, dense buildings and mixed traffic make single-station centralized perception unreliable, motivating distributed heterogeneous sensing for non-cooperative targets. We present VertiSPOT (Vertiport distributed Sensing and Perception-Oriented Testbed), a high-fidelity Unreal Engine (UE)–Simulink co-simulation testbed that integrates city-scale scenes, occlusion-aware raycasting, realistic UAM traffic scheduling, and configurable camera, LiDAR, and radar deployments. We formulate sensor deployment as visibility-aware optimization with trajectory priors and provide a realistic vertiport case study to validate deployment and perception strategies. VertiSPOT supports synchronized multimodal acquisition, automatic annotation of 2D and 3D bounding boxes, and standardized interfaces to benchmark sensor deployment strategies and distributed perception strategies with edge–cloud collaboration. In a detailed urban region of more than two square kilometers, we collect over 36000 synchronized time steps, yielding over 806000 labeled images with 3.8 million 2D boxes and 548000 valid 3D boxes for six aircraft categories. We report stage-wise and end-to-end evaluations using representative 2D and 3D detectors to quantify sensing coverage, perception accuracy, and multimodal complementarity.
